item.title: Balu Forge Q2 Consolidated Net Profit Jumps 18%; Board approves ₹162 crore Warrant Issue to Promoters
item.description:
Balu Forge Industries Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of ₹76.59 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 17.8% from the same quarter last year. Revenue from operations rose 8.3% year-on-year to ₹324.34 crore.

Total income for the quarter grew 9.1% to ₹330.27 crore. Profit before tax rose 13.4% to ₹90.61 crore, and profit growth outpaced revenue growth because of improved margins. Net profit margin on operating revenue widened to about 23.6% from 21.7% a year earlier. Basic earnings per share rose 8.4% to ₹6.59.

The half-year numbers show stronger momentum. Consolidated revenue from operations for April-September 2026 rose 17.3% year-on-year to ₹625.05 crore, while total income grew 18.1% to ₹634.85 crore. Profit before tax for the half year rose 14.3% to ₹171.34 crore, and net profit climbed 16.9% to ₹142.68 crore. Half-year basic EPS stood at ₹12.08, up 12.3%.

On a sequential basis, the second quarter was also stronger than the first. Revenue grew about 7.9% over the June quarter, and net profit rose roughly 15.9% from ₹66.09 crore.

The company's costs rose faster than revenue in several areas. Total expenses for the quarter rose 7.5% to ₹239.65 crore, but the cost of materials consumed climbed 14.5%. Employee benefit expenses jumped 39% and depreciation rose about 66%, reflecting the company's expanded asset base after heavy capital spending. Finance costs rose nearly 35%, in line with higher borrowings. Other expenses were up 15.1%.

The foreign subsidiary, Safa Otomotiz FZE-LLC, was a major contributor to the group's performance, according to figures disclosed in the auditor's report. It reported revenue of ₹128.98 crore and net profit of ₹32.71 crore for the quarter. That is roughly 40% of consolidated revenue and about 43% of consolidated net profit. For the half year, the subsidiary posted revenue of ₹255.78 crore and net profit of ₹61.62 crore.

Standalone performance was also strong. Standalone revenue from operations for the quarter rose 17.1% to ₹195.44 crore, and profit before tax grew 21.5% to ₹61.29 crore. Standalone net profit surged 32.8% to ₹47.26 crore, aided by a lower deferred tax charge. For the half year, standalone revenue rose 16.9% to ₹370.45 crore and net profit grew 22.2% to ₹85.05 crore. Standalone basic EPS for the quarter was ₹3.89, up 24.7%.

Warrant issue to promoters

Alongside the results, the board approved a preferential issue of up to 30 lakh fully convertible warrants to two promoters at ₹540 per warrant, including a premium of ₹530. The issue would raise up to ₹162 crore. The issue price is not below the floor price determined under Chapter V of the SEBI ICDR Regulations.

The proposed allottees are promoters Trimaan Jaspalsingh Chandock and Jaikaran Jaspalsingh Chandock, who would receive 15 lakh warrants each. Trimaan currently holds 25.76 lakh shares (2.12%) and Jaikaran holds 25.10 lakh shares (2.07%). Assuming full allotment and conversion, with no other change in share capital, their holdings would rise to 3.28% and 3.22% respectively.

Each warrant can be converted into one equity share of ₹10 face value, in one or more tranches, within 18 months of allotment. 

The board also approved raising the authorised share capital from ₹125 crore to ₹132 crore. This will be done by creating 70 lakh additional equity shares, taking the total authorised shares from 12.5 crore to 13.2 crore.

item.title: Ashok Leyland Q2 Consolidated Revenue Jumps 35% to ₹17,030 Crore; Profit Up 8.8%
item.description:
Ashok Leyland reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹17,029.87 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 35.4% from ₹12,576.86 crore a year earlier. Consolidated profit after tax rose 8.8% to ₹891.45 crore, from ₹819.70 crore in Q2 FY26. Profit before tax grew 14.5% to ₹1,287.16 crore. The year-ago PBT was depressed by a ₹40 crore exceptional charge, and before exceptional items the growth was a more modest 10.6%.

Consolidated earnings per share stood at ₹1.43, up 10.9% from ₹1.29. Total income, including other income, grew 35.1% to ₹17,173.68 crore.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue was ₹30,099.46 crore, up 23.9% year-on-year. Net profit rose 5.5% to ₹1,559.22 crore, and PBT grew 11% to ₹2,236.88 crore.

Commercial Vehicles Drive Growth, Finance Arm Lags

The commercial vehicle business drove the quarter. Revenue from the CV segment surged 39.1% to ₹14,746.97 crore, and segment profit before interest and tax rose 18.8% to ₹1,084.26 crore. The financial services segment grew more slowly: revenue was up 15.7% at ₹2,283.74 crore, while segment profit fell 28.1% to ₹153.27 crore. Impairment loss allowance and write-offs relating to financing activities rose 34.2% to ₹463.48 crore, and consolidated finance costs increased 16.6% to ₹1,343.64 crore.

Volume growth was strong. Commercial vehicle sales rose 32% to 64,677 units from 49,116 units a year earlier. Medium and heavy commercial vehicle (MHCV) volumes grew 44% to 37,958 units, ahead of industry growth of 39%. Domestic MHCV truck volumes were up 48%, against industry growth of 41%. Light commercial vehicle volumes rose 21% to 21,371 units, and exports gained 7% to 5,102 units. Domestic truck market share improved by 1.5 percentage points to 31.5%, excluding Defence. The company said it held its share in buses, excluding EV buses. In LCVs, its VAHAN market share in addressable segments improved 0.3 percentage points to 13.6%.

Standalone Performance

On a standalone basis revenue from operations rose 39.4% to ₹13,364.28 crore and profit after tax grew 12.7% to ₹869.02 crore. Standalone PBT rose 13.9% to ₹1,187.27 crore, and EPS climbed 13% to ₹1.48. EBITDA grew about 16% to ₹1,350 crore, but the margin slipped to 10.1% from 12.1%. The company attributed the revenue gain to strong demand, better price realisation and mix. Cost of materials consumed rose 46.6%, faster than revenue, and other expenses were up 35.8%. Employee costs rose a more modest 9.5%. Standalone other income fell 51.8% to ₹64.94 crore. For the half year, standalone revenue grew 25.6% and net profit rose 8.3% to ₹1,478.12 crore.

The company said it ended the quarter with net cash of ₹3,546 crore, against ₹990 crore a year ago. Chairman Dheeraj Hinduja said the record performance reflects the strength of the company's business fundamentals, competitive product portfolio and customer focus. He added that the international business and Switch Mobility, the electric mobility arm, are progressing well.

Managing Director and CEO Shenu Agarwal pointed to market share gains and fifteen consecutive quarters of double-digit EBITDA margins. He said the cash position gives the company flexibility to invest in new technologies and products. The company also said it introduced new offerings across tippers, buses, haulage and LCVs, and that its distribution expansion is running ahead of plan.

The board declared an interim dividend of ₹1 per equity share of ₹1 face value, or 100%, for FY27. The record date is Friday, November 20, 2026, and the dividend will be paid on or before December 13, 2026.

Auditors have disclaimed a conclusion on the consolidated Q2 results due to unresolved discrepancies in loan balances at material subsidiary Hinduja Leyland Finance, whose financial impact is yet to be determined. The company said the differences are unlikely to materially affect the subsidiary’s financial health or debt-servicing ability.

item.title: Mahindra Logistics Appoints Mohammed Turra as MD & CEO, Hemant Sikka to Step Down
item.description:
Mahindra Logistics has appointed Mohammed Turra as its next Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, succeeding Hemant Sikka, who will step down from the role on December 15, 2026, to pursue other professional interests.

Turra will join the company as an Additional Director and MD & CEO designate from November 16, 2026, and assume the MD & CEO role on December 16, 2026. His five-year term will run until December 15, 2031, subject to shareholder approval.

Turra has been Managing Director and CEO of Mahindra First Choice Wheels (MFCW) since October 2024, where he has led the growth of the group's multi-brand used-vehicle platform. An alumnus of IIM Bangalore, he has over 28 years of experience across industry and consulting, having worked with Boston Consulting Group, Unilever, IBM and Alstom in India, the Middle East, Europe and the US.

He joined the Mahindra Group in 2016 as part of its Group Strategy Office and subsequently led Quiklyz, the leasing business of Mahindra Finance, before taking charge of MFCW.

Sikka's resignation follows a 26-year association with the Mahindra Group. He will cease to be MD & CEO and a director of Mahindra Logistics at the close of December 15, 2026, while his last working day with the company will be December 23, 2026.

During his tenure, Sikka held several leadership positions, including President of the Farm Equipment Sector and Head of Manufacturing at Mahindra's Automotive Sector. Mahindra Logistics said the company had improved profitability under his leadership, with a renewed focus on customer orientation, execution and process simplification.

Mahindra Group Chairman and CEO Anish Shah said Turra would bring strategic insight and execution focus to the logistics business as it enters its next phase of growth.

item.title: Pavna Industries Q2 Revenue Surges 48% to ₹110 crore, Reports ₹1.19 Crore Net Loss
item.description:
Pavna Industries Limited posted a 48.5% year-on-year jump in consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, but fell into a loss. Revenue was ₹110.09 crore, against ₹74.15 crore in the same quarter last year. The company reported a consolidated net loss of ₹1.19 crore (after share of associates), against a profit of ₹1.68 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, revenue rose 19.8% from ₹91.88 crore in the June quarter, while profit swung from ₹87.76 lakh to the loss.

Consolidated profit before tax was a loss of ₹1.28 crore, against a profit of ₹2.87 crore a year ago and ₹1.55 crore in the June quarter. The tax line gave some relief, with a net tax credit of ₹24.28 lakh against a tax expense of ₹1.19 crore last year. Total comprehensive income was a loss of ₹1.19 crore, against a profit of ₹2.01 crore.

Costs grew much faster than sales. Total expenses rose 54.6% to ₹111.56 crore from ₹72.15 crore. Cost of materials consumed more than doubled, up 106.3% to ₹79.74 crore from ₹38.64 crore. Finance costs rose 126.1%, and other expenses climbed 35.4% to ₹17.02 crore. Other income collapsed 77.4% to ₹19.58 lakh from ₹86.74 lakh.

Some lines moved the other way. Purchase of stock-in-trade fell 13.7% to ₹8.79 crore. Employee benefits expense dropped 33.3% to ₹4.68 crore from ₹7.02 crore, and was also down from ₹6.95 crore in the June quarter. The company built up inventory worth ₹6.15 crore during the quarter, against ₹1.24 crore a year ago.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue rose 50.1% to ₹201.96 crore from ₹134.56 crore. Profit was almost wiped out. Profit before tax and exceptional items fell 92.5% to ₹27.23 lakh from ₹3.63 crore. Last year's half-year included a ₹2.58 crore exceptional item, and on that basis profit before tax fell 74.2% from ₹1.06 crore. After tax and the share of associates' losses, the group posted a net loss of ₹30.91 lakh, against a loss of ₹3.75 lakh a year earlier. Total comprehensive loss was ₹35.08 lakh, against ₹4.65 lakh.

Half-year costs show the same pattern. Total expenses rose 53.2% to ₹202.15 crore, materials consumed rose 105.9% to ₹141.94 crore, and finance costs rose 125.1% to ₹5.63 crore. Other expenses rose 43.9% and depreciation rose 21.3%. Employee costs fell 20.4% to ₹11.63 crore, and other income fell 55.5% to ₹46.18 lakh. The loss attributable to the owners narrowed to ₹34.90 lakh from ₹82.94 lakh, because minority shareholders' share of profit fell sharply to ₹3.99 lakh from ₹79.19 lakh.

The parent company's standalone results showed the same trend. Standalone revenue for the quarter rose 44.6% to ₹103.75 crore from ₹71.72 crore, but the company reported a net loss of ₹1.38 crore against a profit of ₹2.07 crore. Standalone pre-tax loss was ₹2.17 crore, against a profit of ₹3.05 crore. Standalone materials cost rose 75.4% to ₹87.86 crore, and finance costs rose 138% to ₹2.95 crore. Standalone revenue grew 18.5% from the June quarter, when the company had earned ₹88.7 lakh in net profit.

For the half year, standalone revenue rose 47.3% to ₹191.29 crore from ₹129.83 crore. The company made a net loss of ₹49.19 lakh, against a profit of ₹88.26 lakh. Pre-tax loss was ₹78.39 lakh, against a profit of ₹1.75 crore a year earlier, which was struck after a ₹2.49 crore exceptional charge.

item.title: Tolins Tyres Q2 Revenue Jumps 43%; Net Profit Slips 6.5% on Margin Squeeze
item.description:
Tolins Tyres Limited reported a 43.3% year-on-year rise in consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, but profit after tax fell 6.5%. Revenue came in at ₹94.72 crore, against ₹66.10 crore in the same quarter last year. Consolidated net profit was ₹6.50 crore, down from ₹6.95 crore a year earlier. Earnings per share were ₹1.64, compared with ₹1.76, a decline of about 6.8%.

On a sequential basis, the picture was stronger. Revenue grew 19.5% from ₹79.27 crore in the June 2026 quarter, and net profit rose 5% from ₹6.19 crore. Total comprehensive income was ₹6.71 crore, flat against the year-ago quarter.

Profitability was squeezed by costs growing faster than sales. Profit before tax rose 5.6% to ₹8.61 crore from ₹8.16 crore, but net margin narrowed to 6.86% from 10.52% a year earlier. Cost of materials consumed surged 68.1% to ₹81.59 crore, and total expenses rose 47.5% to ₹86.55 crore. Other income fell 40.5% to ₹44.4 lakh. Tax expense climbed 75.6% to ₹2.12 crore from ₹1.21 crore, including an ₹11.3 lakh prior-period tax charge.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue was ₹173.98 crore, up 11.6% from the first half of FY26. Profit after tax fell 22% to ₹12.69 crore from ₹16.26 crore, and profit before tax declined 21.1% to ₹16.49 crore from ₹20.90 crore. Half-year EPS was ₹3.21, down from ₹4.11, a drop of about 21.9%. Net margin for the six months stood at 7.29%, against 10.43% a year earlier. Total comprehensive income was ₹12.93 crore, down 21.7% from ₹16.50 crore.

The growth was driven entirely by the India business. India segment revenue rose 62.3% year on year in the quarter to ₹84.54 crore from ₹52.08 crore, and segment profit grew 35.1% to ₹7.39 crore from ₹5.47 crore. The UAE business, run through Tolins Tyres LLC, went the other way. Its revenue fell 27.4% to ₹10.18 crore from ₹14.03 crore, and segment profit roughly halved, down 50.3% to ₹1.57 crore from ₹3.15 crore. India contributed about 89% of quarterly group revenue, up from about 79% a year ago.

Over the half year, India revenue grew 18.4% to ₹153.81 crore, though segment profit slipped 6% to ₹14.20 crore from ₹15.10 crore. UAE revenue fell 22.1% to ₹20.17 crore, and its segment profit dropped 55.3% to ₹2.95 crore from ₹6.59 crore.

item.title: TIL Limited's Q2 Revenue Jumps 146% to ₹193 crore on Gas Compressor acquisition; Net Loss Narrows
item.description:
Material handling equipment maker TIL Limited reported a more than two-and-a-half-fold rise in consolidated revenue for the September 2026 quarter, helped by the consolidation of its newly acquired gas compressor business, while its net loss narrowed sharply from a year earlier. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 146.5% to ₹192.93 crore in the second quarter, from ₹78.27 crore in the same period last year. Total income, including other income, rose 142.8% to ₹197.79 crore from ₹81.45 crore.

The consolidated net loss for the quarter was ₹1.31 crore, against ₹7.73 crore a year earlier, a reduction of 83.1%. The loss attributable to owners of the company was ₹1.49 crore, down 80.7% from ₹7.73 crore, with non-controlling interests accounting for a profit of ₹0.18 crore. Loss before tax narrowed 85.9% to ₹1.30 crore from ₹9.24 crore. Total comprehensive loss was ₹1.33 crore against ₹7.66 crore, and loss per share improved to ₹0.17 from ₹1.36. Sequentially, revenue grew 64.7% from ₹117.13 crore in the June quarter, while the net loss shrank 76% from ₹5.45 crore.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue from operations rose 119.6% to ₹310.06 crore from ₹141.18 crore a year earlier, and total income rose 107.2% to ₹315.24 crore from ₹152.16 crore. The half-year net loss narrowed 51.5% to ₹6.76 crore from ₹13.95 crore. The loss attributable to owners fell 45.2% to ₹7.64 crore, and loss before tax narrowed 55.9% to ₹8.61 crore from ₹19.53 crore. Loss per share for the half year was ₹0.86, against ₹2.45 in the year-ago period. Total comprehensive loss was ₹6.84 crore, against ₹13.84 crore.

The revenue surge is largely due to the company's acquisition of a 60% stake in Tulip Compression Private Limited, which became a subsidiary with effect from May 8, 2026. TIL paid ₹119.01 crore to Gainwell Commosales Private Limited for the 37,90,250 shares, following shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting on March 14. The new "Packaging, Erection, Commissioning and O&M of Gas Compressors" segment contributed ₹92.27 crore of revenue in the September quarter and ₹130.79 crore in the half year, with segment profits of ₹0.82 crore and ₹3.15 crore respectively. The subsidiary's auditors reported a net profit after tax of ₹0.45 crore for the quarter and ₹2.19 crore for the half year.

The legacy Material Handling Solution business also grew. Segment revenue rose 28.6% to ₹100.66 crore in the quarter from ₹78.27 crore, and 27.0% to ₹179.27 crore in the half year from ₹141.18 crore. The segment's loss before tax narrowed 44.8% to ₹6.85 crore in the quarter from ₹12.42 crore. For the half year it narrowed to ₹16.81 crore from ₹30.51 crore. On a standalone basis, quarterly revenue was ₹100.66 crore, up 28.6%, and total income rose 29.6% to ₹105.52 crore. The standalone net loss fell 77.9% to ₹1.71 crore from ₹7.72 crore, and the half-year standalone loss narrowed 36.4% to ₹8.87 crore from ₹13.94 crore.

Costs rose in line with the larger operating base. Consolidated total expenses grew 119.4% to ₹198.96 crore in the quarter. Cost of materials consumed rose 123.8% to ₹108.86 crore, and employee benefit expense rose 56.9% to ₹19.47 crore. Other income rose 52.8% to ₹4.86 crore from ₹3.18 crore.

item.title: Warburg Pincus to Acquire 38.51% Stake in Pricol’s Demerged Electronics Business
item.description:
Pricol Limited and global private equity firm Warburg Pincus have entered into definitive agreements for the latter to acquire the promoter group’s entire 38.51% stake in Pricol Autotech Limited, which will house Pricol’s Driver Information and Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business. The DICVS business reported revenue of around Rs 2,400 crore in FY26, accounting for approximately 60% of Pricol’s consolidated revenue.

Pricol had announced the proposed demerger of its Driver Information and Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business into Pricol Autotech on 27 June 2026. Once the scheme takes effect, Pricol Autotech is expected to be listed on the NSE and BSE.

Following the listing, Warburg Pincus will acquire the Mohan family promoters’ 38.51% holding in Pricol Autotech and launch a mandatory open offer to public shareholders. The open offer will cover up to an additional 26% of the company’s share capital. Upon completion of the transaction, Warburg Pincus will become Pricol Autotech’s largest shareholder.

Pricol Autotech will house the DICVS business, which manufactures driver information systems and automotive electronics, including instrument clusters, telematics, sensors and e-cockpit solutions. The business supplies original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and off-highway segments.

The DICVS business reported revenue of approximately Rs 2,400 crore in FY26, accounting for around 60% of Pricol’s consolidated revenue. Its separation into an independent listed entity is intended to provide the business with a dedicated platform to pursue growth opportunities in India and international markets.

The transaction marks a change in ownership for Pricol’s automotive electronics business, while the promoter family will retain control of the remaining operations. Following the demerger, Pricol Limited will continue to operate its Actuation, Control and Fluid Management Systems (ACFMS) business. Its polymer products business will operate through wholly owned subsidiary Pricol Precision Products Private Limited. Both businesses will remain under the ownership and management of the Mohan family, with no change in their shareholding.

Vikram Mohan, Chairman and Managing Director of Pricol Limited, said the demerger would provide Pricol Autotech with greater focus and independence to pursue its growth plans. He said Warburg Pincus’ automotive sector experience, resources and international network would support the business in its next phase. Pricol Limited, meanwhile, will continue to focus on developing its retained businesses.

Anish Saraf, Managing Director at Warburg Pincus, said the investment would build on Pricol Autotech’s existing OEM relationships, engineering capabilities and product development strengths. He added that the firm would work with the management and employees to support the company’s long-term plans and expand its presence in domestic and international markets.

Swapnil Sinha, Managing Director at Warburg Pincus, said automotive electronics presented investment opportunities as vehicle technologies become more sophisticated. The firm plans to support Pricol Autotech through investments in technology and talent, expansion of capabilities and customer relationships, and strategic acquisitions.

Warburg Pincus said the transaction would support the evolution of Pricol Autotech into a broader automotive electronics business. The company’s product portfolio and customer base across multiple vehicle segments are expected to provide a platform for expansion.

item.title: TVS Srichakra Q2 Profit Surges to Rs 44.4 crore, Revenue Jumps 37%
item.description:
TVS Srichakra Ltd, the maker of Eurogrip tyres, reported a 305.4% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 44.43 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, against Rs 10.96 crore in the same quarter last year. Revenue from operations rose 37.4% to Rs 1,272.63 crore from Rs 926.49 crore. Total income grew 37.2% to Rs 1,275.03 crore.

Profit before exceptional items and tax rose 179% to Rs 57.96 crore from Rs 20.77 crore, while profit before tax climbed 214.5% to Rs 57.27 crore from Rs 18.21 crore. Profit attributable to owners of the group was Rs 44.43 crore, up 299.9% from Rs 11.11 crore. Earnings per share, basic and diluted, rose 299.6% to Rs 58.02 from Rs 14.52. Total comprehensive income was Rs 43.97 crore, compared with a negative Rs 2.92 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, revenue was up 19.2% from Rs 1,067.61 crore in the June quarter, and net profit rose 30.6% from Rs 34.02 crore.

For the half year ended September 30, 2026, consolidated revenue from operations grew 34.0% to Rs 2,340.24 crore from Rs 1,745.90 crore. Net profit stood at Rs 78.45 crore, up 229.8% from Rs 23.79 crore, and profit before tax rose 168.8% to Rs 102.51 crore from Rs 38.13 crore. Half-year EPS was Rs 102.45, up 226.9% from Rs 31.34. The company booked a net exceptional charge of Rs 1.69 crore in the half year, whereas the year-ago period carried a net exceptional gain of Rs 15 crore. Before exceptional items and tax, profit rose 350.5% to Rs 104.20 crore from Rs 23.13 crore.

Total consolidated expenses rose 33.9% to Rs 1,217.07 crore from Rs 908.65 crore, growing slower than revenue. Cost of materials consumed climbed 58.7% to Rs 773.31 crore, other expenses rose 34.6% to Rs 269.98 crore, and employee benefits expense grew 10.0% to Rs 119.57 crore. Depreciation and amortisation was up 6.0% at Rs 37.71 crore, while finance costs fell 8.9% to Rs 11.32 crore from Rs 12.42 crore. 

On a standalone basis, Q2 revenue from operations rose 35.9% to Rs 1,175.91 crore from Rs 865.04 crore, and net profit rose 118.5% to Rs 34.55 crore from Rs 15.81 crore. Standalone profit before tax was Rs 46.00 crore, up 116.8% from Rs 21.22 crore, and EPS rose to Rs 45.12 from Rs 20.65. For the half year, standalone revenue was Rs 2,173.27 crore, up 33.6% from Rs 1,626.78 crore, and net profit was Rs 63.77 crore, up 87.9% from Rs 33.93 crore. Half-year standalone EPS was Rs 83.28 against Rs 44.31.

Balance sheet and cash flow

Consolidated total assets stood at Rs 3,265.06 crore as of September 30, up from Rs 3,042.88 crore at March 31, 2026. Total equity rose to Rs 1,239.97 crore from Rs 1,190.18 crore.

  • Trade receivables: Rs 580.51 crore, up 41.4% from Rs 410.46 crore at March-end, broadly in line with the surge in sales
  • Inventories: Rs 634.86 crore, down from Rs 742.21 crore
  • Borrowings: Rs 237.99 crore non-current and Rs 540.83 crore current, against Rs 269.91 crore and Rs 492.60 crore at March 31
  • Cash flow from operations (H1): Rs 181.01 crore, down from Rs 206.38 crore a year earlier
  • Capital spending (H1): Payments for acquisition of assets rose 79.2% to Rs 127.19 crore from Rs 70.97 crore

item.title: Mahindra’s Auto Reorganisation: Who Leads Sales, EV Marketing and Manufacturing?
item.description:
Mahindra & Mahindra is redrawing the reporting lines of its automotive business from April 1, 2027, under R Velusamy, President of the Automotive Business. Shuchi Suri will report to Velusamy as Chief Sales & Marketing Officer, Automotive Business, as automotive division CEO Nalinikanth Gollagunta moves to group corporate development.

The November 5 internal announcements say the heads of SUV and commercial vehicle product planning, manufacturing operations and the Nagpur greenfield project will also report directly to Velusamy. Gollagunta, whose automotive remit covered manufacturing, sales, marketing and customer care, will take charge as Executive Vice President & Head of Corporate Development in Worli, reporting to Group CEO and Managing Director Anish Shah.

Shah said the group would identify a “potentially significant new growth opportunity that merits focused evaluation” and asked Gollagunta to lead its evaluation and development.

Sales, marketing and charging under Suri

Suri, currently Executive Vice President, Mahindra Experiences, joined the group in May 2026 after more than 22 years at Unilever, where she was most recently Global Vice President for Homecare.

“She will lead Sales, Marketing, Customer Care, Charging Infrastructure and Accessories Business,” Velusamy said in his announcement to employees.
Pavan Kumar will oversee sales, customer care and customer experience for passenger and commercial vehicles. Reeti Nageshri, who previously led business operations and strategy at Mahindra Electric Automobile Ltd (MEAL), will head marketing and specialist sales for electric SUVs. Both will report to Suri.

Anoop Kachhara, who was appointed to lead EV charging infrastructure in January 2026 with a reporting line to Gollagunta, will now report to Suri. The change puts charging infrastructure and specialist electric SUV sales under the same executive.

Neha Anand will lead marketing for the XUV 7XO and XUV 3XO, AmritaRamanathan for the Thar and Scorpio, and Mahesh Kulkarni for the Bolero and light commercial vehicles below 3.5 tonnes. Mohit Vini will lead accessories, while Sailesh Sahu will oversee strategic sales and operations planning analytics. The marketing services role, covering consumer insights, media buying, PR, CRM and digital, is listed as vacant.

How the EV subsidiary fits in

Velusamy is also Managing Director of MEAL. The subsidiary’s sales head, Deepak Sinha, will report to both Nageshri and Kumar. Kumar will continue to oversee MEAL’s customer care and dealer operations, including dealer financing, dealership infrastructure, network expansion and compliance.

MEAL’s product planning, finance and HR leads will have dual reporting lines to their counterparts in the wider automotive business. Shruti Agarwal, who leads product planning at MEAL, will also report to Jogindra Shetti, who heads SUV product planning for the wider automotive business.

Product Planning and Nagpur Report Directly to Velusamy

Shetti and Satish Karandikar, who leads commercial vehicle product planning, will report directly to Velusamy.

Rajesh Jejurikar, Executive Director and CEO of the Auto & Farm Sector, said the company’s manufacturing plans include “adding capacity at our existing manufacturing sites” alongside developing the Greenfield site in Nagpur.
Vinay Khanolkar will lead the Nagpur project through the start of production, while Nasir Deshmukh will continue to lead automotive manufacturing operations. Both will report directly to Velusamy.

item.title: BYD's Denza Eyes 80-100 Sales in Two Months, Plans Six-City Retail Expansion
item.description:
BYD's luxury electric vehicle brand Denza expects to convert an initial pipeline of around 80-100 vehicle reservations into sales over the next two months as it prepares to open exclusive showrooms across six Indian cities following the launch of its D9 and Z9 GT models on Friday.

The Chinese automaker has introduced the seven-seater D9 electric luxury MPV at Rs 90 lakh and the Z9 GT performance electric car at approximately Rs 1.57 crore (ex-showroom). Both models will be imported into India as completely built units (CBUs).

Speaking at a media roundtable on the sidelines of the launch, BYD India management said early customer interest had been encouraging, although it was too soon to provide a firm sales target.

"For the next couple of months, we should be doing 80-100 odd cars," Rajeev Chauhan, Senior Vice President, EPV Business, BYD India**, said**, adding that the estimate was based on initial reservations and feedback from dealer partners.

The company clarified that these were prospective orders rather than confirmed deliveries. Management said pricing and customer preferences would influence how many reservations eventually translate into sales.

Denza expects a waiting period of approximately three to four months for orders requiring specific exterior colours and interior combinations. However, the company has already imported some vehicles to support early deliveries.

Rajeev Chauhan, identified as Vice President of BYD India's electric passenger vehicle business, said the company expected to reduce delivery timelines as orders and customer preferences became clearer.

To support the launch, Denza will establish exclusive retail outlets in Gurugram, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai and Ahmedabad. The showrooms will operate separately from BYD's existing passenger vehicle network, with dedicated sales and service facilities.

According to management, the first outlets will begin operations shortly, with the six-city rollout expected to be completed over the next 30-45 days. Existing BYD dealer partners will support the expansion.

The launch places Denza in India's small but growing luxury vehicle market. The D9 will compete with premium MPVs such as the electric MG M9, Toyota Vellfire, Mercedes-Benz V-Class and Lexus LM. The Z9 GT, meanwhile, has no direct rival in India but will compete for buyers considering high-performance luxury EVs such as the BMW i5 M60.

BYD management said it expects the D9 to generate higher volumes, while the Z9 GT will help establish Denza's positioning in the performance luxury segment.

The luxury brand's entry comes as BYD's existing India passenger vehicle business continues to expand. According to VAHAN registration data compiled by Flash Finance, BYD recorded 6,379 passenger vehicle registrations during January-October 2026, an increase of approximately 35% over the corresponding period last year. The company has crossed 20,000 cumulative vehicle sales in India since entering the passenger vehicle market and currently operates approximately 50 BYD showrooms.

With Denza, the company is now looking to expand beyond its existing electric passenger vehicle portfolio into higher-priced luxury categories. However, management said it would assess the response to the two models before committing to additional products, import volumes or local manufacturing investments.

item.title: Electric Motorcycle Adoption Will Take More Time: Royal Enfield CEO
item.description:
Royal Enfield expects electric motorcycles to take longer to gain widespread acceptance and plans to expand its Flying Flea electric mobility business gradually, even as customer interest in its first model, the C6, continues to grow.

The Eicher Motors-owned motorcycle maker said enquiries for the Flying Flea C6 have been encouraging in India and international markets, but bookings are converting more slowly as customers take time to experience and understand the new category.

Speaking during Eicher Motors' Q2 FY27 earnings conference call on Friday, Royal Enfield Chief Executive Officer B. Govindarajan said the company was focused on developing the electric motorcycle market rather than pursuing rapid expansion. "We are not in any rush. We wanted to build that properly, one by one," Govindarajan said.

He explained that while electric motorcycles are gaining interest among urban commuters, adoption for wider applications could take longer. Unlike electric scooters, which are largely used for daily commuting, motorcycles serve a broader range of riding requirements.

"So, the adoption, in my personal view, will take more time," he said, adding that there was no clear basis for predicting whether adoption would accelerate within three or five years.

The comments come at a time when India's electric two-wheeler market is recording strong growth, although the transition continues to be driven overwhelmingly by scooters rather than motorcycles.

According to VAHAN data, India’s electric two-wheeler market witnessed strong growth in FY27, with retail registrations rising approximately 70% year-on-year to 13.48 lakh units during April-October 2026, compared with around 7.91 lakh units in the corresponding period of FY26. However, the market has been dominated by electric scooters, with TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto, Ather Energy and Hero MotoCorp’s VIDA collectively accounting for the majority of registrations during the period.

Royal Enfield's assessment suggests that manufacturers entering the electric motorcycle segment may need more time to develop consumer acceptance, particularly among buyers who use motorcycles for longer journeys and recreational riding.

Flying Flea Expands Across India and Europe

Royal Enfield has delivered around 200 Flying Flea C6 electric motorcycles in India since the model's launch in April 2026, according to CEO B. Govindarajan. Customers have collectively ridden more than 1.25 lakh kilometres on the motorcycle.

The C6 was initially introduced in Bengaluru before being expanded to Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai. Its planned retail and service network now covers 40 touchpoints across the four cities, including dedicated stores and outlets operating alongside existing Royal Enfield dealerships. The company now plans to make the electric motorcycle available in Delhi.

Despite encouraging customer interest, Govindarajan said bookings were progressing more slowly as buyers took time to experience and understand the new category. "The enquiries are very good. Bookings are slower because we have to give more experience to them," he said.

Priced at ₹2.79 lakh (ex-showroom), the C6 comes with a 3.91kWh battery and offers a claimed range of 154km. Royal Enfield also offers a Battery-as-a-Service option, reducing the upfront vehicle price to ₹1.99 lakh, with battery subscription charges payable separately.

Meanwhile, the company has also expanded Flying Flea into Europe and the UK, introducing the C6 in Paris, Barcelona, Rome, Berlin and London in September 2026. The rollout is being undertaken in phases, with an emphasis on establishing sales, service and ownership support.

Govindarajan said the initial response in Europe had been encouraging, with bookings recently opened in international markets. However, the company plans to expand gradually while ensuring that the necessary retail and service infrastructure is in place.

New Models to Support Long-Term Growth

Royal Enfield is also expanding its electric motorcycle portfolio. At the EICMA motorcycle exhibition in Milan earlier this month, the company showcased the Flying Flea S6, a scrambler-style electric motorcycle developed on the same platform as the C6.

The S6 is scheduled to be launched in the summer of 2027. The motorcycle is designed for urban riding as well as light off-road applications, expanding Flying Flea's appeal beyond conventional city commuting.

Govindarajan said the company would continue developing additional electric motorcycles as it prepares for the longer-term transition towards electric mobility.

However, he maintained that the pace of expansion would depend on how quickly consumers adopt the technology and how effectively the company can establish the ownership experience.

"But we are in for a long haul. We want to build the category," he said.

item.title: Royal Enfield Fast-Tracks Capacity Expansion as Bookings Rise 21%, Dealer Stocks Fall to One Week
item.description:
Royal Enfield is bringing forward the second phase of its manufacturing capacity expansion in Tamil Nadu as motorcycle bookings grew around 21% year-on-year and dealer inventories remained at just 7-8 days, reflecting strong demand that continues to outpace production.

The Eicher Motors-owned motorcycle maker is accelerating work on the second module of its Cheyyar brownfield expansion, which will increase its annual manufacturing capacity from the current 16.5 lakh motorcycles to 18 lakh units by the fourth quarter of FY27. The company is attempting to begin production from the additional capacity as early as January 2027.

The third and final module is scheduled to become operational in the second quarter of FY28, taking Royal Enfield's combined annual manufacturing capacity to 20 lakh motorcycles ahead of the following year's festive season.

"We are now working on bringing forward the Module 2," B. Govindarajan, Managing Director of Eicher Motors and CEO of Royal Enfield, said during the company's Q2 FY27 earnings conference call on Friday.

The accelerated expansion comes as Royal Enfield struggles to fulfil growing orders despite increasing production. Govindarajan said the company entered the festive season with significantly lower dealer inventory after retail sales outpaced supplies during the first few months of the financial year.

Dealer stocks currently stand at approximately 7-8 days, including motorcycles in transit, against the company's normal operating inventory of three to four weeks. Production has increased around 15% year-on-year, but supplies have remained insufficient to meet demand.

"The retail for the season was limited only by the supplies," Govindarajan said.

To improve vehicle availability during the festive period, Royal Enfield increased direct shipments to dealers from around 1-2% of dispatches to approximately 18%. The move helped reduce delivery delays by limiting the time motorcycles spend moving through the distribution network.

The company now plans to rebuild dealer inventories over the next two months while continuing to fulfil pending orders.

According to Govindarajan, bookings have increased approximately 20-21% year-on-year during the financial year to date, with growth during the festive period slightly higher. Some motorcycle models have pending orders equivalent to approximately two months of sales, although the company did not disclose its overall order backlog.

Importantly, management said demand remained healthy even after the festive season. Enquiries and bookings have returned to their pre-festive growth trend, indicating that customer interest has not weakened sharply following Diwali.

The company expects the increased production capacity to help clear pending orders and support further growth in wholesale dispatches. It also plans to increase marketing activities once vehicle availability improves.

Sales Rise 18% During April-October FY27

Royal Enfield's manufacturing expansion comes against the backdrop of strong domestic sales growth.

The motorcycle manufacturer’s total dispatches increased 18% year-on-year to 8,42,538 units during April-October FY27. Domestic sales increased 20% year-on-year to 7,63,548 motorcycles, while exports remained largely flat at 78,990 units, compared with 78,528 units a year earlier.

In October alone, Royal Enfield recorded its highest-ever monthly dispatches of 1,33,442 motorcycles, an increase of 7% over the corresponding month last year. Its September-October dispatches totalled 2,67,400 motorcycles, supported by festive demand.

The strong domestic performance has kept pressure on the company's manufacturing operations, with management indicating that additional supplies could support higher sales in the coming months.

Manufacturing Capacity to Reach 24.5 Lakh Units by FY30

Royal Enfield's immediate expansion is part of a broader manufacturing investment programme aimed at increasing capacity across its Indian operations.

In February this year, Eicher Motors announced an investment of Rs 958 crore for the brownfield expansion at its Cheyyar facility in Tamil Nadu. The project was designed to raise overall annual capacity from approximately 14.6 lakh motorcycles to 20 lakh units in phases by FY28.

The company began FY27 with an annual capacity of approximately 15 lakh units, following improvements in productivity, automation and the removal of production bottlenecks at its existing operations.

The first module of the Cheyyar expansion became operational during the second quarter, increasing installed capacity to 16.5 lakh units. With the second module now being advanced, the company expects another 1.5 lakh units of annual capacity by Q4 FY27, followed by an additional 2 lakh units by Q2 FY28.

Beyond the Tamil Nadu expansion, Royal Enfield is also developing a greenfield manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh. In May, the company announced plans to invest approximately Rs 2,500 crore in a phased project at Tada, near Tirupati. Subsequently, in July, Eicher Motors' board approved Rs 1,225 crore for the first phase.

The first phase will add annual capacity of 4.5 lakh motorcycles at full utilisation and is expected to be completed during FY30, subject to market conditions. Once operational, Royal Enfield's total annual manufacturing capacity across its Indian plants will reach approximately 24.5 lakh motorcycles.

For the immediate future, management's priority remains increasing production, clearing pending orders and rebuilding dealer inventories before stepping up efforts to generate additional demand.

"We have to fill that inventory," Govindarajan said, adding that the company was sitting on substantial bookings and would focus on increasing supplies over the coming months.
item.summary: <![CDATA[The motorcycle maker is advancing its Cheyyar expansion to raise annual capacity to 18 lakh units by Q4 FY27 and 20 lakh by Q2 FY28, as strong bookings continue to outpace production.]]>

item.title: VECV Rides Light-duty Truck Surge and Shifting Export Corridors to Highest-ever Second-quarter Sales
item.description:
VE Commercial Vehicles Ltd., the truck- and bus-making joint venture between Eicher Motors Ltd. and Sweden’s AB Volvo, reported a 37% jump in second-quarter net profit on Friday, buoyed by record vehicle dispatches, a 29% surge in engineering component sales and sustained fleet replacement demand across urban and rural India.

Net profit for the July–September quarter (Q2FY27) rose to Rs 341.6 crore, up from Rs 249.3 crore in the same period a year earlier, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer B. Srinivas told reporters during a post-earnings conference call. Revenue from operations increased 24% year-on-year to Rs 7,568.6 crore from Rs 6,105.8 crore.

"Revenue from operations rose 24% year on year, and profit after tax grew 37% over the same period, a result that reflects disciplined execution that overcame supply chain challenges and inflation pressures linked to the lingering West Asian crisis. During the quarter, we reaffirmed our commitment to deliver industry-leading uptime to Eicher truck and bus customers with the inauguration of our state-of-the-art Uptime Next Center in Pithampur,” Srinivas said in a press release.

Light-Duty Momentum and Second-Half Demand Outlook

VECV dispatched 28,071 vehicles during the second quarter, up 28.2% from 21,901 units a year earlier, marking its highest-ever second-quarter volume. That took cumulative first-half (April–September 2026) deliveries to 52,886 vehicles, a 21.5% increase over the prior year’s first half.

Monthly wholesale disclosures from the VECV Newsroom show that domestic Eicher-branded truck and bus dispatches climbed 32.2% year-on-year during the quarter to 25,638 units, accelerating from 7,575 units in July and 7,584 units in August to 10,479 units in September—before adding another 9,676 domestic units in October.

Responding to a question during the call on whether infrastructure spending is sustaining heavy-tonnage truck orders into the second half of the fiscal year, Srinivas said demand remains broad-based across geographies and payload categories, with light- and medium-duty (LMD) trucks slightly outpacing heavy-duty haulage.

"In H1, we have grown with a speed of 21.5%, and it is all across the segments, both light and medium duty and heavy-duty trucks. However, the traction is slightly more as far as the light and medium duty is concerned," Srinivas said. "However, the demand across rural, semi-urban and urban markets, as well as across all segments, is offering a great amount of growth opportunities. So at this point in time, our estimate is that the growth momentum of H1 will continue in H2 also."

Electric Pro X Milestone

In the small commercial vehicle (SCV) category, where VECV entered the 3- to 3.5-tonne segment in 2025 to compete in last-mile e-commerce and cold-chain logistics, cumulative sales of the Eicher Pro X range crossed 5,000 units during the quarter. Srinivas disclosed on the call that battery-electric variants accounted for more than a quarter of those initial dispatches.

"The recently launched Eicher Pro X crossed 5,000 in cumulative sales, reflecting encouraging customer acceptance and confidence in the Eicher brand. Of these, over 1,400 units are electric," Srinivas said.

At the top end of the passenger carrier market, Srinivas revealed that Volvo Buses India logged its highest-ever six-month volume as private intercity fleet operators upgraded to multi-axle sleeper and seater coaches. "Volvo Buses India delivered a record 422 units in the first half of the year and has announced significant orders from large operators as passengers move towards comfortable and safe buses," Srinivas said.

Export Realignment Amid West Asian Shipping Bottlenecks

While India’s overall commercial vehicle exports rose 72.5% in the July–September quarter, according to Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) data, VECV’s Eicher-brand exports slipped 5.9% year-on-year in the second quarter to 1,715 units (470 in July, 578 in August and 667 in September), before rebounding 30% year-on-year to 911 units in October.

Asked during the call about geopolitical headwinds and container availability, Srinivas said that while specific overseas markets faced disruptions from the West Asian conflict, the shifting trade landscape had opened new export destinations across Africa, the Middle East and other emerging markets. "We are getting good traction, particularly in some of the African countries and our traditional markets where we are exporting. However, there is a change in the overall spectrum of exports. So it is actually providing new opportunities," Srinivas said, adding that VECV holds a "healthy order book with us, both in trucks and buses."

Pressed to elaborate on how the export order book is shifting, Srinivas said VECV is engineering market-specific variants across both steering configurations to capture post-crisis demand. "We find a lot of newer opportunities emerging post the current ongoing crisis," Srinivas said. "We are exploring the new markets which are coming up where, in terms of appreciation for the Indian products, both in terms of right-hand drive and also left-hand drive. At the same time, we are also coming up with some new products which are very exclusive to some of these markets in terms of overall customer value proposition."

Components Surge 29%, Ujjain AMT Plant on Schedule

Beyond whole vehicles, VECV’s non-vehicle industrial units posted sharp gains in the second quarter. Answering a query on the performance of Eicher Engineering Components and powertrain exports, Srinivas disclosed that the components vertical grew 29% year-on-year during the quarter, while Euro VI engine shipments from the VE Powertrain facility in Pithampur to Volvo Group hubs globally matched overall corporate growth.

"The component business is doing pretty well and it's growing at the speed of 29%, and there is a good amount of opportunities for all the businesses they are serving. The second one is the engine exports; even that business is performing quite well, in line with the overall growth, and the new projects of the other aggregates are also in line with our plans."

Srinivas also confirmed that construction of VECV’s greenfield Automated Manual Transmission (AMT) plant, a Rs 544-crore project at Vikram Udyogpuri near Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, licensed to manufacture Volvo Group’s 12-speed AMT for Asia-Oceania exports and Eicher heavy-duty trucks, remains on schedule. "The plant is going as per the plan at this point of time at our new site near Ujjain, with a capacity of 40,000 transmissions," Srinivas continued.

item.title: Tata Motors Absorbs 60% of Commodity Cost Hit as PV Margins Remain Under Pressure
item.description:
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) is absorbing around 60% of the increase in commodity costs, offsetting the remainder through calibrated price hikes and cost-reduction measures. The pressure is expected to persist through Q3, with the company considering steeper price increases in Q4 to protect margins, according to Dhiman Gupta, CFO, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles. “Of the commodity hit that we've seen, 40% we've been able to offset through the calibrated price increases and cost actions that we've taken. The balance, we continue to absorb in our P&L,” he said.

TMPV reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 20,423 crore in Q2 FY27, up 50.9% year on year, supported by record volumes of over 2 lakh units, a 40% increase over the corresponding quarter last year. However, EBITDA margin declined 180 basis points to 4%, while EBIT margin fell 50 basis points to negative 0.3%. Profit before tax and exceptional items stood at Rs 25 crore, against Rs 156 crore in Q2 FY26. “Commodity inflation had significantly eroded the benefits of operating leverage, pricing actions and cost reductions. Steel, rubber and copper remain key sources of cost pressure and we expect these headwinds to continue into Q3. While steep commodity cost pressures remained a headwind, we responded through calibrated pricing and focused cost actions,” Shailesh Chandra, managing director and CEO of TMPV, said. The company expects to maintain profitability around current levels in Q3, with some improvement in Q4 through a combination of higher price increases and deeper cost-reduction efforts, Chandra added.

Demand Continues to Outstrip Supply

The margin pressure comes at a time when Tata Motors is witnessing strong demand across its portfolio, with the company saying demand continues to exceed supply in certain models and powertrains. Its domestic market share stood at 14.3% in Q2, consolidating its position as India's second-largest passenger vehicle manufacturer. The company also recorded a strong festive performance, with volumes of 75,000 units in August and market share rising to 14.8%. Retail sales during the festive period increased nearly 10% over an already high base in the previous year.

“We are not pursuing market share gains by deliberately holding back price increases, but are focused on fulfilling existing demand and expanding supply. Market share for us is consequential because here we are not trying to buy market share because we are in a situation where demand is significantly exceeding supply and it is about fulfilling the demand,” Chandra said.

Tata Motors plans to scale up production through internal capacity measures and closer coordination with suppliers. However, Chandra said the constraints had not resulted in production losses so far. “There is definitely some level of stress that we have on the semiconductor side, electronic parts. But we are securing the supply or we are paying higher cost for that,” he said.

On the electric vehicle side, the company ended last year at around 14% penetration, he added. “Last quarter, we were at 23% penetration and as you know, we are significantly behind the demand. We are at 10 days of inventory and with significant pending bookings. So the effort is on the supply side. So as we improve the supply in the next two to three months, the share of electric vehicles will also go up,” he said.

EV supply remains a key constraint, with demand significantly outstripping the company’s ability to fulfil orders. Tata Motors is currently meeting only 60-65% of EV demand, despite ramping up monthly supplies from around 9,000 units in March-April to 16,000 units. “All our factories are running at full capacity, if not more, with some plants operating for additional days. In terms of meeting demand, we are currently able to serve only about 60-65% of the total demand for EVs, which is why dealership inventory levels remain very lean. We have significantly ramped up supplies from around 9,000 units a month in March-April to 16,000 units currently, and hope to get closer to 20,000 units a month over the next two to three months. However, demand continues to exceed supply. While our in-house capacity is fungible and we can shift capacity from ICE vehicles to EVs, we are closely working with suppliers on around 26 critical parts to further ramp up supplies,” Chandra added.

Greener Powertrains Cross Half of Sales

The company's electric vehicle business delivered its strongest-ever quarterly performance, with volumes exceeding 47,000 units, up 90% year on year. Tata Motors strengthened its EV market share by 380 basis points sequentially to around 43%, retaining its leadership despite increasing competition and the entry of more manufacturers into the segment.

CNG also recorded its highest-ever quarterly volumes, supported by the company's twin-cylinder portfolio. Together, EVs and CNG accounted for more than half of Tata Motors' overall passenger vehicle volumes.

The shift towards alternative powertrains is gathering pace across the industry. India's passenger vehicle market grew around 29% year on year to approximately 1.36 million units in Q2 FY27. CNG penetration rose to around 25%, while EV penetration reached approximately 8%, taking the combined share of greener powertrains to nearly one-third of industry volumes.

Chandra said the combined share of CNG and EVs had increased from around 20-22% in FY25 to 32-33% currently, largely at the expense of petrol vehicles. Diesel has so far remained relatively stable at 17-18%. The company expects the transition towards greener powertrains to continue, supported by new launches, wider OEM participation and regulatory measures, including the recently notified CAFE III policy.

item.title: Belrise Industries Q2 Net Profit Rises 25.2% to Rs 1,665.47 Million
item.description:
Belrise Industries Limited reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 27,463.82 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 16.7% from Rs 23,535.41 million in the corresponding quarter a year earlier. Consolidated profit for the period was Rs 1,665.47 million, up 25.2% from Rs 1,329.81 million. On the reported figures, this works out to a net profit margin of about 6.1%, compared with about 5.7% a year earlier. The company did not disclose EBITDA in the results filed with the stock exchanges on November 13, 2026. All growth rates and margins in this article are calculated from the reported figures, and all amounts are in Rs million unless stated otherwise.

Consolidated profit before tax was Rs 2,207.48 million, against Rs 1,806.69 million a year earlier, a rise of 22.2%. Total consolidated income, including other income of Rs 362.88 million, was Rs 27,826.70 million, compared with Rs 23,804.50 million. Basic and diluted earnings per share were Rs 1.75, up from Rs 1.63. Compared with the preceding quarter ended June 30, 2026, consolidated revenue rose 7.8% from Rs 25,464.68 million, and profit rose 36.9% from Rs 1,216.67 million.

For the half year ended September 30, 2026, consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 52,928.50 million, up 14.7% from Rs 46,157.48 million in the same period last year. Consolidated profit for the half year was Rs 2,882.15 million, up 17.8% from Rs 2,446.62 million, and profit before tax rose 20.9% to Rs 3,871.24 million from Rs 3,201.91 million. Half-year earnings per share were Rs 3.13, against Rs 2.99. For the year ended March 31, 2026, the company reported consolidated revenue of Rs 95,091.02 million and profit of Rs 4,968.60 million.

On a standalone basis, which covers the parent company alone, revenue from operations for the September quarter was Rs 22,258.46 million, up 23.5% from Rs 18,020.21 million. Standalone profit was Rs 1,587.25 million, up 29.2% from Rs 1,228.63 million, giving a net margin of about 7.1%. Standalone profit before tax was Rs 2,104.84 million, compared with Rs 1,642.88 million. Standalone earnings per share were Rs 1.66, up from Rs 1.50. For the half year, standalone revenue was Rs 43,141.24 million, up 19.8% from Rs 35,999.69 million, and profit was Rs 2,729.94 million, up 21.1% from Rs 2,253.91 million.

Among consolidated costs, the filing shows that finance costs for the quarter fell to Rs 437.10 million from Rs 558.89 million a year earlier, while employee benefits expense rose to Rs 1,222.51 million from Rs 834.15 million. Depreciation and amortisation was Rs 1,027.40 million, compared with Rs 865.37 million. Cost of materials consumed was Rs 18,472.43 million, against Rs 14,583.93 million. Purchase of stock-in-trade was Rs 3,872.03 million, compared with Rs 4,374.47 million. Standalone finance costs were Rs 364.17 million, up slightly from Rs 354.93 million in the year-earlier quarter, while for the half year they fell to Rs 734.51 million from Rs 951.56 million.

The company said its operating segment is "Automotive Components", so segment-wise disclosure under Regulation 33(1)(e) of the SEBI Listing Regulations is not applicable. The results do not include sales volumes or management commentary. The consolidated results include the wholly owned subsidiaries Badve Engineering Trading FZE in the United Arab Emirates, H One India Private Limited and Belrise Defence & Aerospace Private Limited. They also include step-down subsidiaries Belrise SDM in France and Belrise UK Holdings Limited, together with Chester Hall Precision Engineering Holdings Limited and Chester Hall Precision Engineering Limited in the United Kingdom, the last two listed as step-down subsidiaries from April 4, 2026. Subsidiary-level financials were not separately disclosed.

The board, at its meeting on November 13, 2026, approved a fresh Scheme of Amalgamation under which H One India Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, would merge into Belrise Industries on a going-concern basis. The scheme is subject to statutory and regulatory approvals and is proposed to be filed with the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Mumbai Bench. An earlier scheme had been approved by the board on November 11, 2025. The joint statutory auditors, Shailesh Haribhakti & Associates and Rathi Rathi and Co, issued an unmodified conclusion on the results. Their review report included an emphasis of matter on this scheme, noting that H One India's board rescinded the earlier scheme and approved the fresh one on November 6, 2026, and that no effect of the scheme has been given in the results.

The board also approved incorporating a special purpose vehicle under the PM SETU Project and executing a shareholders' agreement for it, and amended the policy on materiality of related party transactions. The company said additional information on the SPV and the amalgamation will be disclosed in due course. The meeting began at 4:05 pm and ended at 5:15 pm (IST).

The results notes also set out several capital and corporate developments during the period. On July 17, 2026, following shareholder approval on July 2, the company allotted 7,72,72,727 equity shares of Rs 5 each at Rs 220 per share under a Qualified Institutions Placement, raising Rs 17,000 million against the up to Rs 20,000 million approved by the board on May 24, 2026. Paid-up equity share capital rose to Rs 4,835.76 million, comprising 96,71,51,919 equity shares. The company reported no deviation in the use of proceeds from its IPO and the QIP for the quarter.

On August 4, 2026, the company entered into a Business Transfer Agreement to acquire the India Tipper Body Business of Hyva (India) Private Limited, a subsidiary of JOST Werke SE, on a slump-sale basis for about USD 5.65 million. Separately, the board approved on January 31, 2026 a scheme of amalgamation involving Badve Autocomps Private Limited, Eximius Infra Tech Solutions Private Limited and Belrise Industries. NSE and BSE issued observation letters dated July 3, 2026 with "no adverse observations", and the scheme was submitted to the NCLT, Mumbai, on September 30, 2026.

At its 30th Annual General Meeting on September 30, 2026, shareholders declared a dividend of Rs 0.55 per equity share for the year ended March 31, 2026, paid on October 15, 2026. They also approved raising the authorised share capital from Rs 500 crore to Rs 550 crore, divided into 110,00,00,000 equity shares of Rs 5 each.

The consolidated balance sheet as at September 30, 2026 showed total assets of Rs 1,09,048.37 million, compared with Rs 85,497.86 million at March 31, 2026. Total equity was Rs 71,271.84 million, up from Rs 52,262.85 million. Consolidated non-current borrowings were Rs 6,560.50 million, against Rs 7,501.80 million, and current borrowings were Rs 6,430.23 million, against Rs 6,889.08 million. Cash and cash equivalents were Rs 10,306.15 million.

In the consolidated cash flow statement for the half year, net cash generated from operating activities was Rs 4,911.51 million, compared with Rs 549.97 million a year earlier. Net cash used in investing activities was Rs 16,725.46 million, including capital expenditure of Rs 6,662.35 million. Net cash from financing activities was Rs 14,060.02 million, which includes Rs 16,265.90 million shown as proceeds from the security premium reserve.

item.title: JLR Cuts FY27 Margin Guidance to 2-3%, Flags £1.25bn Cash Outflow
item.description:
Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has lowered its FY27 adjusted EBIT margin guidance to 2-3% from 4% and expects a free cash outflow of around £1.25 billion, as the British luxury carmaker navigates a challenging global operating environment even as it returns to profitability following last year's cyber-related disruption.

JLR reported revenue of £5.9 billion for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 20% year on year, while first-half revenue increased 3.2% to £11.9 billion. Profit before tax and exceptional items stood at £6 million for Q2, compared with a loss of £485 million in the corresponding period last year. For H1 FY27, the company reported a profit of £115 million against a loss of £134 million a year earlier.

“We have included everything that we know (in our margin guidance). We do know that this market is extremely fast-moving, both in terms of opportunities and in terms of risks related to our launches,” Richard Molyneux, Chief Financial Officer, JLR, said.

JLR recorded a free cash outflow of £540 million during Q2 and ended September with £1.8 billion in cash and total liquidity of £6 billion, including a new £1 billion loan facility signed on September 30. “Of the £530 million of exceptional charges, £295 million relates to the voluntary redundancy programme that we launched in the quarter and relates to circa 4,000 people. This programme itself has attracted the right level of interest and we now have circa 3,000 colleagues who have signed up and will leave the business this financial year,” he added.

The company expects the programme to continue into the next financial year as it moves beyond its launch peaks, with the remaining employee exits expected to be achieved largely through voluntary applications. JLR is targeting £1.7 billion in operational savings over the next two years through business simplification, improved operational performance and cost reductions.

Its five-year investment programme of £15-18 billion remains on track, with £11.5 billion already invested.

Recovery Hinges on New Launches

Despite the financial pressures, JLR is pressing ahead with its product pipeline, particularly its electrification plans. Production of the Range Rover Electric and Range Rover Sport Electric has begun, with customer deliveries expected to start early next year. The company has already received around 5,000 orders for the Range Rover Electric. “We are building Range Rover Sport and Range Rover Sport BEVs. The initial launch vehicles are going to be distributed to the retailers imminently, but it is interesting to note that even without any retail customer ever actually seeing the car, let alone driving it, we already have circa 5,000 orders for Range Rover BEVs,” he said.

The next launch in the pipeline is the Range Rover GT, scheduled to enter production in early calendar 2027 at JLR's Halewood facility in northern England. The new Jaguar Type 01 is scheduled to enter production later in FY28, during calendar 2027.

China remains a challenge

JLR's recovery is also being complicated by persistent weakness in China, where sales of Western luxury carmakers have come under pressure from domestic competitors. The company said sequential wholesale volume growth in the UK and overseas markets helped offset reductions in China and the Middle East. “China is certainly an issue for us.

And the decline that all Western OEMs have seen over there is certainly taking an effect. And I can't guarantee at this stage that we have reached the end point of that decline,” he said. JLR is reassessing its approach to the market while keeping retailer inventory at acceptable levels and avoiding aggressive discounting, according to Molyneux.
item.summary: <![CDATA[Despite returning to profitability in Q2, the British luxury carmaker faces pressure from a weak China market, restructuring costs and global headwinds.]]>

item.title: Eicher Motors Q2 FY2027 Net Profit Rises 14.9%
item.description:
Eicher Motors Ltd reported a 20.3% YoY increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 7,421.72 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY2027), from Rs 6,171.59 crore. Consolidated net profit rose 14.9% to Rs 1,573.37 crore from Rs 1,369.45 crore.

Total expenses rose 21.9% to Rs 5,947.29 crore from Rs 4,878.41 crore. Profit before share of joint venture profit, exceptional items and tax increased 9.9% to Rs 1,806.31 crore. This pre-tax margin, before the joint venture’s contribution, narrowed to 24.3% from 26.6%.

Material costs, comprising raw materials and components consumed, traded goods purchased and changes in inventories, totalled Rs 4,305.71 crore, up 23.9% from Rs 3,474.75 crore. They accounted for 58.0% of revenue against 56.3% a year earlier. Other major expense lines were:

VECV Contribution

Share of profit from joint venture VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV) increased 37.9% to Rs 186.07 crore from Rs 134.91 crore. PBT rose 12% to Rs 1,992.38 crore. Net profit margin narrowed to 21.2% from 22.2%. Basic earnings per share was Rs 57.31 against Rs 49.93.

Standalone revenue from operations rose 21.3% to Rs 7,159.04 crore, and standalone profit for the period increased 9.7% to Rs 1,324.99 crore.

For H1 FY2027, consolidated revenue from operations grew 25.3% to Rs 14,054.14 crore. Total expenses rose 26.4% to Rs 11,288.29 crore. Profit before tax increased 16.2% to Rs 3,917.61 crore, and net profit rose 17.9% to Rs 3,035.88 crore.

Material costs for the half year were Rs 8,185.29 crore, up 30.2%. Depreciation and amortisation rose 35.9% to Rs 540.35 crore, and VECV’s profit contribution rose 21.1% to Rs 353.57 crore.

Consolidated net cash from operating activities increased 38.1% to Rs 3,671.56 crore in H1. The cash flow statement shows trade payables contributed Rs 984.06 crore, against Rs 304.46 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Trade payables to creditors other than micro and small enterprises stood at Rs 3,598.02 crore, up from Rs 2,638.10 crore at March 31, 2026.

Capital expenditure rose 39.4% to Rs 860.29 crore from Rs 616.98 crore. Capital work-in-progress increased to Rs 384.30 crore from Rs 203.08 crore, and intangible assets under development rose to Rs 714.40 crore from Rs 533.22 crore. Dividend paid was Rs 2,251.08 crore against Rs 1,919.95 crore.

item.title: Tata Motors PV Posts Rs 5,451 Cr Q2 Loss as Restructuring Costs, Impairments Mount
item.description:
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPVL, formerly Tata Motors Ltd) reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,451 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27), after booking Rs 6,738 crore in exceptional losses.

The charges relate mainly to employee separation costs and asset impairment, and Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) accounts for Rs 6,793 crore of them. Consolidated revenue rose 34% year-on-year to Rs 96,920 crore, and profit before exceptional items and tax was Rs 403 crore.

The financials of the company should be seen in the context of  a continuing operations basis. The headline year-ago net profit had stood at Rs 76,248 crore due to a one-time Rs 82,616 crore accounting gain from the demerger of its commercial vehicles business.

The company reported a consolidated loss before tax of Rs 6,335 crore. In Q2 FY26 it recorded a loss of Rs 5,462 crore before exceptional items and tax. EBITDA margin improved 630 basis points to 6.2%, and EBIT margin rose 790 basis points to 1.1%.

The company said the year-on-year improvement mainly reflects recovery from the cyber incident at JLR in the same period last year. Sequentially, it said margins were affected by adverse mix and continuing commodity cost pressures.

The company said the loss after tax was recorded after recognition of a deferred tax asset. The quarter had a net tax credit of Rs 884 crore, including a deferred tax credit of Rs 1,745 crore. 

Exceptional Items

Employee separation cost was Rs 3,776 crore and impairment of assets was Rs 2,856 crore. Rationalisation and restructuring programme costs were Rs 161 crore, partly offset by a past service cost credit of Rs 55 crore, bringing the net exceptional loss to Rs 6,738 crore.

Employee separation costs and asset impairment together account for Rs 6,632 crore. Q2 FY26 exceptional items of Rs 2,608 crore included Rs 2,008 crore of supplier claims and cyber-related incident expenses, along with Rs 840 crore of employee separation cost. The reported loss therefore does not reflect operating performance alone.

Material Costs

Combined material costs, comprising cost of materials consumed, purchase of products for sale and changes in inventories, rose 35.6% year-on-year to Rs 65,022 crore in Q2 FY27, from Rs 47,946 crore a year earlier. The cost of materials consumed was Rs 58,825 crore and purchases of products for sale were Rs 5,330 crore. Changes in inventories added Rs 867 crore. 

Material costs equalled 67.1% of revenue from operations, against 66.3% in Q2 FY26, a rise of about 80 basis points. Material costs grew slightly faster than the 34.0% increase in revenue.

Sequentially, combined material costs rose 7.9% from Rs 60,245 crore in Q1 FY27, against a 1.2% increase in revenue. The ratio to revenue increased by about 420 basis points from 62.9%.

The Q1 figure included a Rs 5,474 crore inventory build that reduced reported costs, whereas Q2 recorded an inventory-change charge of Rs 867 crore. This movement is consistent with the company's reference to adverse mix and commodity pressures, though the results do not separate the effects.

For H1 FY27, combined material costs were Rs 125,267 crore, up 20.8% from Rs 103,681 crore. That equals 65.0% of revenue, against 64.8% a year earlier. The balance sheet shows inventories at Rs 56,755 crore as of September 30, up from Rs 50,126 crore at March 31.

JLR's Q2 revenue rose 20.3% to £5.9 billion, and H1 revenue rose 3.2% to £11.9 billion. EBITDA margin was 6.6% and EBIT margin was 1.1%. Profit before tax and exceptional items was £6 million in Q2 and £115 million in H1, against losses of £485 million and £134 million a year earlier.

JLR said wholesale volumes grew quarter-on-quarter in the UK and overseas markets, offsetting reductions in China and the Middle East. It recognised £530 million in exceptional items, covering restructuring, separation costs and write-downs of intangible assets under development and other assets.

JLR revised its full-year guidance to an adjusted EBIT margin of 2-3% and a free cash outflow of about £1.25 billion. It cited market challenges, geopolitical risks and the exceptional costs recognised in the quarter. Free cash outflow was £540 million for the quarter, and total liquidity was £6.0 billion at September 30. The revised guidance is a more material development than the year-on-year recovery.

PB Balaji, Chief Executive Officer of JLR, said: “JLR delivered positive operating profits in the second quarter and first half of the financial year, despite ongoing global challenges.”

Tata Passenger Vehicles reported revenue of Rs 20,423 crore, up 50.9% and, according to the company, its highest ever for a quarter. Volumes grew 40% and EV volumes grew 90%.

Margins declined despite the growth. EBITDA margin fell 180 basis points to 4.0% and EBIT margin fell 50 basis points to negative 0.3%. Profit before tax and exceptional items was Rs 25 crore, against Rs 156 crore in Q2 FY26. The company attributed the pressure to adverse commodity and foreign-exchange movements.

Shailesh Chandra, Managing Director and CEO of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, said: “While steep commodity cost pressures remained a headwind, we responded through calibrated pricing and focused cost actions.”

Consolidated free cash flow was negative Rs 6,300 crore in Q2. Net debt was Rs 50,800 crore at September 30, 2026. Cash and cash equivalents fell to Rs 10,925 crore from Rs 22,880 crore at March 31, while non-current borrowings rose to Rs 74,314 crore from Rs 44,248 crore.

Tata Passenger Vehicles generated free cash flow of Rs 825 crore in Q2 and Rs 1,945 crore in H1. It ended the quarter with net cash of Rs 7,900 crore, comprising cash of Rs 11,000 crore and gross debt of Rs 3,100 crore. The group's cash outflow is concentrated in JLR.

Standalone Results

On a standalone basis, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported revenue from operations of Rs 19,201 crore and a net profit of Rs 3 crore. The standalone notes disclose a Rs 50 crore reversal of provisions for gratuity and long-term compensated absences.

The company had charged Rs 123 crore in FY26 under the new Labour Codes, mainly because of the revised definition of wages. Changes in salary structure during the quarter led to the reversal, which was recorded as an exceptional gain. It is a one-off accounting benefit and does not reflect a change in the vehicle business.

Outlook

The company said global geopolitical volatility, luxury-segment demand, the pace of EV adoption and commodity costs remain key factors to monitor. For JLR, it said near-term priorities are building sales momentum from new EV launches and showing progress on its Enterprise Missions plan, which targets £1.7 billion of savings over two years.

Dhiman Gupta, Chief Financial Officer of TMPVL, said: “In Q2 FY27 TMPV continued to build on its strong momentum in the domestic business, while JLR delivered resilient volumes despite global market specific challenges and wind-down of previous Jaguar models. However, adverse mix and persistent commodity pressures weighed on margins. Both businesses remain fundamentally strong, and we stay focused on executing our medium-term priorities: driving growth through new launches, accelerating cost reductions and improving cash generation.”

item.title: JSW Motors Partners With AWS To Host Connected-Car Data In India
item.description:
JSW Motors, the passenger vehicle arm of the JSW Group, has partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to host its connected-car platform on servers located in India. The arrangement will ensure that data generated by its connected vehicles, including driving and location data and footage from in-car cameras, is stored within the country.

The company said all data stored on the platform will remain under its ownership and control. Data handling will be governed by JSW Motors' security policies and applicable Indian legislation, including the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

The connected-car system will also involve Indian technology and telecommunications partners. Tata Elxsi is supporting the localisation of the telematics control unit (T-Box), which connects the vehicle to the cloud, while Airtel will provide the network infrastructure for vehicle connectivity.

The partnership combines AWS's cloud infrastructure with local data storage as connected vehicles increasingly generate information on driving patterns, vehicle usage and location.

JSW Motors is preparing to launch its first passenger vehicle, which will be manufactured at its facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra.
